5acd4878c5d8ed8cd596822e7d400bb9924b27da: The Fiss ski area, with its 186 km of runs, offers a fine choice for every type of skier: large enough not to go round in circles for a week, yet compact enough to find your favourite sectors easily. The 38 lifts let you link descents without long queues. Fiss has kept the identity of an authentic mountain village, far from the concrete resorts of the 1970s. People come here for the clean air, unspoiled scenery and a friendly atmosphere that stands apart from the industrialisation of skiing in some large ski areas. With a summit at 2828 m and a village at 1438 m, snow cover in Fiss is generally reliable from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause problems early in the season, but the situation recovers quickly with the first serious snowfalls. Budgeting for a stay in Fiss is clearly on the high side: the day lift pass costs 78€, on top of accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence, but you should be aware of it before you go. In short: Fiss keeps its promises. A resort in the Northern Alps that will suit most skiers without disappointing them.

5ae773f66c19665d589ef1a38d2e509c98316423: Hoch-Imst is a low-key resort on a modest scale: 10.3 km of pistes for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. The family reputation of Hoch-Imst is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. The altitude of Hoch-Imst (1053 m at the base, 2026 m at the top) helps it maintain decent snow cover through the depths of winter. January and February are the most reliable; in December and March, it is worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. At 47€, the day lift pass places Hoch-Imst among the intermediate resorts on budget: neither cheap nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and its facilities justifies this price for most skiers. In short: Hoch-Imst does not rival the giants of skiing, and does not pretend to. It is an honest destination, often underestimated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
